\begin{center}
{\LARGE\bfseries Jessica L. Burnett, Ph.D.}\\[2pt]
Washington, DC \textbar{} (720) 730-0974 \textbar{} jessica.burnett@nasa.gov\\
Program Executive, Earth Science Data Systems, NASA Headquarters \textbar{} GS-0801-15
\end{center}

# Summary

Program executive for NASA's operational Earth science data production portfolio (\textasciitilde\$40M/yr), working where data infrastructure, open science policy, and real-world data use meet. Oversees data systems run by civil servant and contractor teams at four NASA centers; serves as Data Systems Lead for 11 satellite missions and airborne campaigns; negotiated the agreement standing up a new Goddard project office. Contributed to SMD's Scientific Information Policy (SPD-41a) and puts it into practice daily. Former research ecologist and open-source software developer; joined NASA as an AAAS Science & Technology Policy Fellow.

# Professional Experience

**Program Executive, Earth Science Data Systems (ESDS)**, Earth Science Division, Science Mission Directorate\
NASA Headquarters, Washington, DC \textbar{} Nov 2024 -- Present \textbar{} GS-0801-15

Programmatic lead for Foundational Data Products (FDP), the Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS), the Land, Atmosphere Near-real-time Capability for Earth Observations (LANCE), Science Investigator-led Processing Systems (SIPS), and the Earth Science Information Partners (ESIP) cooperative agreement. These systems produce global Earth data used by scientists, firefighters, land managers, and the public.

- **Program and budget oversight.** Lead annual planning, budget allocation, and performance review for a \textasciitilde\$40M/yr portfolio across four geographically dispersed NASA centers, holding projects to cost, schedule, and technical performance while balancing Headquarters requirements with each project's mission and user commitments.
- **New program formulation and agreements.** Leading formulation of FDP, which moves data processing to the cloud and consolidates production efforts, from concept to a leadership-approved framework (definition, designation criteria, product specifications, portfolio management). Negotiated the agreement with Goddard Space Flight Center to stand up the new FDP project office, covering scope, roles, governance, and resources. Consolidating existing production work into an FDP budget more than 20\% smaller than its current cost; reused NASA's Senior Review framework for FDP evaluation instead of building a new process.
- **Open science in practice.** As Data Systems Lead on the HQ Mission Management Team for 11 satellite missions and airborne campaigns, hold oversight authority for each mission's Open Science and Data Management Plan. Portfolio defaults to open-source software and open data, with exceptions only where controlled or sensitive information requires them.
- **Metrics-driven investment.** Leading the use of data usage metrics across the ESDS portfolio to guide Earth Science Division investment priorities, center-level engagement, and partnership opportunities, including which data products FDP will designate.
- **Data governance.** Leading an effort to define what "authoritative data" means for the Earth Science Division and SMD, connected to interagency standards work through the Federal Geographic Data Committee.
- **Accountability for operational systems.** Brought HQ accountability to two long-running near-real-time systems (LANCE and FIRMS) that had operated with minimal HQ oversight: required their first formal project plans, made Earth Action (the other key HQ stakeholder) a co-signatory, and required it to fund non-data-system work such as science and outreach, cutting ESDS's share of those costs by about half. Now extending the model to NASA Black Marble.
- **Data management capability.** Requested a capability to track dependencies among SIPS-produced data products; the ESDIS Project built it into a full knowledge graph and management system that gives the program visibility into upstream and downstream dependencies and now informs continuity risk management and FDP priorities.
- **Leading through influence.** Over more than a year, moved Goddard's Earth Sciences Division (Code 610) and the ESDIS Project (Code 423) from limited coordination to a working partnership on LANCE and FIRMS; the two organizations now place staff on each other's subproject leadership teams. Scoping a joint NASA--NOAA approach to Level-0 data reprocessing to reduce duplicate interagency spending.
- **People and talent.** Oversee about 10 civil servants in center project offices, who in turn manage contractor teams, setting priorities and reviewing deliverables; selected the FDP Project Manager; mentor and delegate portfolio workstreams to an AAAS Science & Technology Policy Fellow; mentor 1--2 NASA interns each year. Identified the AAAS fellowship as a new way to bring talent into ESDS, now in use.

**Program Coordinator, Ecological Conservation (AAAS Science & Technology Policy Fellow)**, Earth Science Division\
NASA Headquarters, Washington, DC \textbar{} Aug 2022 -- Nov 2024

- **Interagency agreements.** Built the relationships behind a binding Memorandum of Understanding among USGS, NASA, and the National Park Service, and a new center-to-center partnership between USGS Patuxent Wildlife Research Center and NASA Goddard.
- **Competitive awards.** Managed the solicitation lifecycle for NASA Ecological Conservation awards: drafted solicitation language (including open-data requirements), ran peer review panels, and supported selections.
- **National representation.** Represented NASA on the National Nature Assessment federal steering committee, the National Invasive Species Council, the natural capital accounting interagency working group, and the National Plan for Civil Earth Observations writing team.
- **Strategy and community.** Led development of the program's strategic and business plan guiding 1- and 3-year investments; organized national workshops of 75--500 participants.

**Research Ecologist and Mendenhall Postdoctoral Fellow**, U.S. Geological Survey, Lakewood, CO \textbar{} Aug 2019 -- Aug 2022

- Developed statistical methods and open-source software that put large national monitoring datasets into wider use; lead developer of `bbsAssistant` (USGS software release; *Journal of Open Source Software*), which opened North American Breeding Bird Survey data to wildlife managers and researchers.

**Earlier Research Positions**

- **Graduate Research Assistant**, Nebraska Cooperative Fish & Wildlife Research Unit, University of Nebraska--Lincoln \textbar{} 2015 -- 2019. Managed concurrent multi-partner research projects; trained state natural resource agency staff in data management and geospatial analysis.
- **Young Scientists Summer Program Fellow**, International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis, Laxenburg, Austria \textbar{} 2018. Selected from over 500 international applicants.

# Open Science and Software

Author or co-author of five open-source R packages for ecological data access and analysis \textbar{} Reviewer, *Journal of Open Source Software* and *ReScience* \textbar{} Selected publications: *Ten simple rules for creating a scientific web application* (2021); *Paths to computational fluency for natural resource educators, researchers, and managers* (2021); *Priorities for synthesis research in ecology and environmental science* (2023)
